runners_data.name: Kodi Fire

runners_data.note: An eight-year-old veteran with honest recent form at this trip on good ground, but the redistribution note is honest — he is a true hold-up type who will struggle if forced forward against his nature; trainer Patrick Chamings has 0 wins from 7 runners in 14 days and a 7-day turnaround flags a quick return that warrants caution.

runners_data.name: Pentonville
runners_data.note: Sharp in current form with a win at Wolverhampton then placed twice since, and his good-ground record at 8f is the most encouraging in the field (3 from 5 on similar going); a 3-year-old carrying 5lb less than his rating peers and ridden by Mr Henry Callan — he is the horse most likely to press forward if no other runner does.

runners_data.name: Palazzo Persico
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 10f on soft ground, which is a different test to today's 8f on good; a genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield through redistribution, meaning his natural tendency to come late may not be fully exploited, and his Flat form at Brighton specifically is untested.

runners_data.name: Endowed
runners_data.note: A 263-day layoff is the most glaring flag in the race — his recent wins came over 6f on good ground, a very different test to today's mile, and the redistribution to midfield means this nine-year-old is unlikely to get his true hold-up berth; headgear not flagged, trainer Flint has 0 from 9 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field (OR 51) with a recent unseated-rider blot on his card and no wins from 15 on similar going; a true hold-up type pushed into midfield by redistribution, and the visor/tongue-tie combination suggests connections are searching for a solution — hard to recommend in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: With all six runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this Brighton mile is set to be run at a crawl early before developing into a sprint finish from the home turn. The pace map cannot accommodate every hold-up type at the rear, meaning Darvel, Palazzo Persico, Endowed, and Wrist Art are all racing out of their natural role — whichever of these gets shuffled forward against their instincts will be doing so reluctantly. Kodi Fire and Pentonville, as the highest-rated hold-up types with the most compelling recent form, are the most likely to sit closest to whatever modest pace materialises and time their runs best. The field holds more genuine closers than can all queue at the rear, and the horses most likely to secure a workable position from the outside are Kodi Fire (proven at the trip on good ground) and Pentonville (in sharp current form); this race shape strongly favours horses with a late turn of foot who can pick their moment in a compressed finish, making the most progressive and recently active hold-up types the primary beneficiaries.

watchPoints.text: Kodi Fire — watch for him to be produced widest of all in the straight; if the field clusters on the rail as expected, his jockey James Hills has the tactical nous to angle out early and secure a clear run to the line.

Pentonville — if he drifts to the front through a vacuum in the early stages, monitor whether Mr Callan allows him to take control or panics and drops him back; either decision materially changes the race shape.

Darvel — a 7-day turnaround for an eight-year-old with 0 trainer wins in 14 days; watch the market carefully pre-race, as any significant drift may signal the quick return is opportunistic rather than confidence-driven.

Endowed — 263 days off the track is the single biggest unknown; watch his paddock behaviour and early running style, as a hold-up horse returning after nine months in a slowly-run race may simply not get competitive in time.

Palazzo Persico — Tony Carroll has 7 wins from 62 runners in 14 days (a healthy yard strike rate); if Palazzo Persico is well-backed despite the drop in trip, treat that as meaningful given the trainer's current form.

races.paceDynamic: Night Bear is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4f Brighton circuit on Good ground. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up types — Amber Honey, Power Of Prayer, Koko Blue, Sarangpur, Suitcase Smith, La Trinite, Douglas Dc, and Gearing's Point — meaning the closers will have to come from behind a horse setting its own terms. Brighton's undulating, turning track and a steady pace set by a single front-runner will compress the field and make it difficult for deep hold-up horses to generate enough momentum late, especially when multiple rivals are competing for the same late ground. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently or in the first third of the pack, as the lone pace-setter is unlikely to be pressured into setting up a race for finishers. Note that Sarangpur, Suitcase Smith, La Trinite, Douglas Dc, and Gearing's Point are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the field holds far more rear-end types than the race shape can accommodate; of these, none is expected to secure a prominent pitch, leaving Night Bear with a near-uncontested lead.

watchPoints.text: Night Bear's early lead is the race-defining factor — if anything pushes forward to challenge Doughty's mount in the first two furlongs, the entire pace structure changes and hold-up horses become live dangers.

La Trinite returns from 333 days off for Mike Murphy; watch the pre-race market and paddock — a short price on a first-day-back horse of this profile would be a significant stable signal worth noting.

Koko Blue's noted tendency to fade in the finish combined with a slow pace that could intensify the closing burst makes her a risk to stay on, despite the course form — watch if she starts to drop out inside the final furlong.

Multiple hold-up horses (Sarangpur, Suitcase Smith, Douglas Dc, Gearing's Point) will be competing for the same ground late; monitor how Dougie Costello positions La Trinite early, as his experience may allow him to steal a march on the others from the rear.

Power Of Prayer's record of 0W1P from 2 runs on Good going at 10f trips is the most directly comparable form in the field — watch whether Jack Callan elects to track Night Bear from an early stage rather than dropping in behind.

races.paceDynamic: Rockafeller Skank is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, comfortable gallop from the front over the 1m2f trip on Good turf at Brighton. The pace is therefore likely to be honest but controlled — Rockafeller Skank sets the tempo entirely on its own terms, which at this course and distance can mean the race is run at a measured clip that preserves energy for the home straight. Masqool, Twilight Guest, and Dogged are all genuine hold-up horses but are mapped to midfield because the field contains more rear-runners than can realistically track that far back in a six-runner field — none of them is likely to get into their true natural position. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or a horse capable of tracking just off a lone leader in a truly uncontested scenario, meaning Rockafeller Skank and any horse with the pace to press from the front are ideally placed, while deep closers must generate their own momentum against a controlled, unexposed gallop.

watchPoints.text: Rockafeller Skank carries 143lbs and has run three times in 15 days — monitor in the paddock for any signs of fatigue before committing to the uncontested lead narrative.

Lucky Sevens with Billy Loughnane is the one horse capable of tracking Rockafeller Skank closely from the outset — if it slots into second early, the race becomes a two-horse contest well before the straight.

Masqool and Twilight Guest are both genuine hold-up horses unable to get their true position in a six-runner field — if they drop to the back anyway, they will face a stern task generating momentum against a controlled pace.
West Hill Rosie's fade-in-finish flag is a live concern over 1m2f on Good — watch for her weakening sharply in the final two furlongs regardless of her early position.
Tony Carroll runs two horses (Masqool, Dogged) in the same race — stable tactics worth monitoring in the paddock to see which, if either, receives more positive pre-race signals.

runners_data.name: Virtue Chastity

races.paceDynamic: The Wicked Wolf is the sole confirmed front-runner and, coming off a 255-day absence, will need to find her rhythm quickly — but with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should be able to dictate an honest, uncontested gallop over this 1m2f Brighton trip on Good turf. Man Is King is the most likely horse to press from a prominent position, with Oj Lifestyle operating from further back as the primary hold-up runner with genuine class claims. The field carries a significant overload of hold-up types: Lenny's Spirit, Gretna Dreams, Danehill Star and Virtue Chastity are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots on the map because there is no room for all of them to race from their natural rear position, meaning several will inevitably end up closer than preferred and will not get the true end-to-end run they need. With one front-runner setting a sustainable pace unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or a well-positioned closer capable of tracking the tempo and kicking on the undulating Brighton camber — not deep closers dependent on being produced last of all, since the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to produce a true late swoop.

watchPoints.text: The Wicked Wolf's 255-day layoff is the biggest tactical unknown — if she blows up before the final furlong, the entire race shape collapses and Man Is King is gifted a straightforward win.

With Lenny's Spirit, Gretna Dreams, Danehill Star and Virtue Chastity all wanting to race from the rear, watch for a traffic bottleneck and scrimmaging in the early-to-mid portion of the race that could shuffle hold-up types even further back than intended.

Man Is King runs just six days after his last outing — watch whether he travels sweetly in the early stages or shows signs of fatigue before the final climb; if he is not travelling by halfway, his chance evaporates.

Brighton's undulating camber and uphill finish favour horses that travel into the race rather than those making ground from a long way back — any hold-up horse needing a strong pace to arrive is vulnerable if The Wicked Wolf keeps things moderate.

The Crisford-trained Extraterrestrial is the one hold-up type with the most realistic claim to a genuine late run, given Jack Callan's 3lb claim effectively brings the horse into the race at a competitive weight — monitor whether he gets a clear passage from two furlongs out.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Sandman is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-strong field and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, is likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over Brighton's undulating 7f. The bulk of this field — Barnsnape Boy, Shes Got The Blues, Spirited Dancer and Skyolaire among the natural hold-up types who retain their rear position — will be looking to close from off the pace, but the modest gallop Mister Sandman sets may not generate enough of a true end-to-end test to fully suit deep closers. The field holds considerably more prominent and hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; of those redistributed, Fai Fai (non-runner), Embarked, Mokata and She Went Whoosh are the ones most likely to have pressed for a forward berth, but with Fai Fai out and the others genuine hold-up types, Mister Sandman's lead looks uncontested. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or track the leader in the first two or three, as a lone front-runner at a measured pace on Good ground at Brighton creates a platform for a well-timed stalker to pounce rather than rewarding extreme late finishers.

watchPoints.text: Barnsnape Boy is the key pace watcher — if he travels smoothly in the slipstream of Mister Sandman through the first half-mile, his recent 7f Good win and strong sim-going profile make him the most dangerous horse in the race.

Mister Sandman's ability to control the pace without being pressured is critical; if he fails to stride away cleanly from the gates and loses the lead, the entire shape of the race collapses and the probability of Scenario A drops sharply.

Shes Got The Blues carries the classiest recent form in the field — a 7f Good win — and Billy Loughnane is a top booking; watch whether she can travel close enough to the pace to land a challenge, as her hold-up style is a risk in a slowly-run race.

My Boy Jack's 117-day absence and switch from Standard to Good turf makes him a significant unknown; if he shows sharp early movement suggesting fitness, he could outrun his odds, but the layoff is a genuine concern in a field of this size.

Scott Dixon saddles three runners (Embarked, My Mate Beattie, She Went Whoosh) — watch market moves on all three at final declarations, as stable form, jockey instructions and potential stable orders across a trio could influence how each is ridden.

runners_data.name: Moulin Booj
runners_data.note: Sole win in last five came over 5f on standard ground and the good surface here suits; a natural hold-up runner under Liam Wright (5lb claim), it needs a proper pace injection to land its challenge and the lone front-runner scenario makes that far from guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Hoodie Hoo
runners_data.note: Charles Hills-trained confirmed pace-setter with tongue-tie, dropping slightly in class here; four of five recent runs have been over 6f so the step back to 5½f is a mild query, but Jason Watson can time the front-running move and an uncontested lead on good ground is very much in its favour.

runners_data.name: The Thames Boatman
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes yard in strong form (4/24 T14) and this horse has won and placed repeatedly over 5f on good ground, including a recent Brighton win; a genuine prominent type whose natural position is easily secured here, and Finley Marsh has the course intelligence to press forward without overdoing it.

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on good at Lingfield and has strong course-form credentials at this sort of trip, but Billy Loughnane will find its natural front-running berth occupied by Hoodie Hoo; its best form comes when leading, and having to race in a less forward position than ideal is a genuine concern with 53 days off the track.

runners_data.name: The Flying Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer has been busy (6/32 T14) and the horse carries blinkers, having shown some ability over this course and distance previously; sits naturally at the back under Mason Paetel (5lb claim) and its best chance comes from a race that falls apart late — an unlikely scenario with Hoodie Hoo dominating.

runners_data.name: Correspondence
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's four-year-old is in decent form (1-2 in last three completed runs) on good ground and over the right trip, but its true running style is more forward-going than its mapped midfield position suggests; Myla Coppins (7lb claim) on a low draw must manage a position that doesn't entirely suit, and the style displacement tempers confidence despite the raw form figures.

races.paceDynamic: Hoodie Hoo is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only five rivals in a six-runner field, should be able to bowl along at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Brighton's 5½f without anyone genuinely testing that position. The Thames Boatman is also a prominent-type but is unlikely to take on Hoodie Hoo early, instead sitting just off the pace; Rogue Bullet is a natural front-runner mapped to midfield because there are more speed-hungry types than slots available, meaning it may end up racing less freely than it wants. The hold-up quartet of Moulin Booj, The Flying Seagull and Correspondence are true finishers but will need the pace to be honest enough to reel in Hoodie Hoo from off the bridle — with only one genuine gallop-setter, that gap may never fully materialise. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel just behind the leader and produce a smooth, decisive move around the final two furlongs, rather than those relying on a strong pace collapse that a lone uncontested front-runner is unlikely to provide. The field holds more prominent and front-running types than can physically occupy those positions; Hoodie Hoo is virtually certain to lead, and The Thames Boatman, with its recent good-ground course form, is best placed to hold the second slot.

watchPoints.text: Hoodie Hoo goes unchallenged to the front — if Jason Watson gets a clean break and no rival contests the lead in the first furlong, the race may effectively be over early on this flat, fast-ground surface.

Rogue Bullet's draw and break — Billy Loughnane will instinctively try to push forward; if it fires out of the stalls and forces Hoodie Hoo wider or faster, pace dynamics shift materially and the entire scenario map changes.

The Thames Boatman's position at the two-furlong mark — if Finley Marsh has it travelling sweetly just behind Hoodie Hoo rather than chasing it, it is a live threat; if it gets shuffled back or meets traffic, its chance is gone.

Moulin Booj's run style dependency — Liam Wright must get a clear sightline through in the last furlong, but with only six runners the field may fan wide enough on good ground; watch for whether it gets a clean passage or is forced to switch.
